tickets.title: Crate Specification Foundation — Purpose, Non-goals, Compliance & Functional Requirements
tickets.background: Architectural foundation of the siprs crate. N0002 defines M20 implementation priorities across all RFC sections. N0003 establishes the Tauri integration boundary and non-goals. N0004 provides domain terminology. N0005 defines compliance requirements (MSRV, target OS, PJSIP version pinning). N0007 enumerates the 15 normative functional requirements. N0008 defines the complete module tree layout and design rationale for single-crate architecture. These specification nodes share no direct implementation files but collectively form the design baseline that all implementation nodes depend on.
scope: M20 implementation priority map with P0-P3 prioritization and design decision cross-references (Q1:A-Q14:A)
Crate non-goals document: SIP server, PBX, RTP stack, recording, GUI, persistence, billing, video — all excluded
Tauri integration boundary: siprs provides Rust-native API only; Tauri ipc::Channel/JS communication is adapter responsibility
Domain terminology glossary (Client, Account, Call, Media Session, Source, Chunk Pair, Raw SIP Event)
Compliance requirements: MSRV 1.95, tokio async, PJSIP 2.17 pin, target OS triple (Windows x86_64, macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64)

15 functional requirements: multi-account, dynamic add/remove, register, UDP/TCP/TLS transports, ICE, PCMU/Opus codecs, DTMF 3-way, event bus, audio pipeline, mixer, Result<T, SipError> API, Send+Sync
Module tree: src/ (client, config, account, call, transport, event, error, audio/, ffi/, runtime/, util/) + build.rs + vendor/
testUnit: UT: Verify all 15 functional requirements can be traced to corresponding RFC sections
testExceptions: Specification-level documentation nodes have no executable test code; coverage is via cross-reference verification
